summary:
Climate Signal is an interactive web platform that lets anyone investigate how our planet is changing, one location at a time—with no coding or scientific background required. Users simply click any spot on an interactive 3D globe or 2D satellite map, or select climate-sensitive presets like the Arctic, Amazon, or Sahara, to analyze up to four decades of NASA satellite and reanalysis observations (1985–2025) across six variables: air temperature, precipitation, soil wetness, solar radiation, relative humidity, and wind speed.

Because natural seasonal cycles—such as summer heat and winter cold—can disguise or exaggerate multi-decade shifts, Climate Signal removes the monthly seasonal cycle and applies rigorous non-parametric statistics (Theil-Sen slope, Hamed-Rao modified Mann-Kendall test, and block-bootstrap confidence intervals) to separate statistically significant trends from natural variability. By turning raw NASA data into clear visual diagnostics and plain-language verdicts, it gives students, researchers, and decision-makers a reliable way to distinguish lasting environmental trends from normal seasonal rhythm.
details:
Climate Signal pairs interactive spatial exploration with rigorous time-series climate statistics. Users select any location via a rotating 3D orthographic globe or a 2D satellite and terrain map that highlights the exact NASA spatial grid cell (~0.5° × 0.625° MERRA-2 or ~1° × 1° CERES). The platform queries the NASA POWER API in real time for monthly records between 1985 and 2025, removes the recurring annual seasonal cycle by computing monthly anomalies, and evaluates long-term change using a Theil-Sen median slope (resistant to extreme weather outliers), a Hamed-Rao modified Mann-Kendall test (accounting for month-to-month autocorrelation), and a 12-month moving-block bootstrap for 95% confidence intervals. Results are presented through interactive deseasonalized trend plots, raw monthly charts, an early-versus-recent period comparison using Welch's t-test, downloadable CSV tables, and an independent spot-check against NASA Giovanni exports for the Svalbard preset.

We built the application in Python using Streamlit (with custom CSS and embedded JavaScript for smooth 60 fps globe rotation and drag handling), Plotly for the 3D globe and interactive time-series charts, Folium (streamlit-folium) for dual-layer Esri satellite and OpenStreetMap views, and NumPy, Pandas, SciPy, and pymannkendall for statistical modeling, backed by the NASA POWER API and NASA Giovanni.

What makes Climate Signal creative and practical is how it bridges playful global discovery—inspired by Globle's spinning interface—with transparent, honest scientific communication. Rather than overwhelming users with raw NetCDF files or misleading them with naive linear regressions, our team specifically accounted for seasonal persistence, serial autocorrelation, API rate-limiting, and spatial resolution caveats. The platform automatically warns users when selected timeframes are too short (<10 years), flags borderline cases where significance tests and confidence intervals disagree, and clearly explains grid-cell limitations—democratizing NASA Earth science so anyone can explore regional climate trends with confidence.

SI Acknowledgment: AI tools were used to assist with code debugging, UI styling, and text editing; all data and statistical calculations come directly from official NASA POWER and Giovanni datasets.
